attributes.born: 1 January 1957, in Nindjé, Ndom, Sanaga-Maritime Department (Littoral Region).
attributes.died: In the night of 11 to 12 May 2026, in Yaoundé, aged 69, after an illness. Several outlets and the festival itself reported his death.
attributes.film_festival: Founded the Écrans Noirs festival in Yaoundé. The operation began in 1996 and the festival in 1997. He founded the Association Écrans Noirs in 2009, and it was recognised as being of public utility in 2016.
attributes.films: Sango Malo (The Village Teacher, 1990 or 1991, adapted from his own novel), Le Grand Blanc de Lambaréné (1995, some lists say 1994, about Albert Schweitzer), the documentary Musique s'en va-t-en guerre (1997) and Le Silence de la forêt (2003, with Didier Ouénangaré).
attributes.honours: Knight of the Burkina Faso National Order of Merit of the Arts (2009), Knight of the French Order of Arts and Letters (2013) and Knight of Cameroon's Order of Valour (2017).
attributes.last_project: He was preparing the 30th edition of Écrans Noirs when he died.

attributes.founded: 1997, by the filmmaker Bassek Ba Kobhio.
attributes.description: Described as Central Africa's largest cinema event, with film classes held alongside the festival.
attributes.23rd_edition: July 2019, on the theme Women in African cinema.
attributes.ecran_d_or_winners: 2016 Tears of Satan (Hicham El Jebbari, Morocco), 2017 Children of the Mountain (Priscilla Anany, Ghana), 2018 Maki'la (Machérie Ekwa Bahango, DR Congo), 2019 The Mercy of the Jungle (Joël Karekezi, Rwanda), 2020 Heart of Africa (Tshoper Kabambi Kashala, DR Congo), 2021 Annato (Fatima Boukdady, Morocco).

attributes.training: Studied physics at the University of Yaoundé and trained in film editing at the Institut National de l'Audiovisuel in Paris, where he studied semiotics with Christian Metz.
attributes.first_feature: Quartier Mozart (1992), shown at the Cannes Film Festival when he was 25.
attributes.awards: A British Film Institute award in 1993 for Quartier Mozart. A special mention of the Holden Award for best script at Turin in 2005 and the Silver Étalon de Yennenga at FESPACO in 2007, both for Les Saignantes.
attributes.films: Quartier Mozart (1992), Have You Seen Franklin Roosevelt? (1994), Aristotle's Plot (1996), La Grammaire de ma grand-mère (1996), Les Saignantes (2005), Imagine Afrika (2007), Le Président (2013), Les Choses et les Mots de Mudimbe (2015) and Naked Reality (2016).
attributes.le_president: His 2013 film Le Président, a fake documentary satirising leaders who cling to power, is described as banned in Cameroon in 2013.
attributes.teaching: Has taught filmmaking at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and Duke University, and held a Harvard fellowship in 2023 to 2024.
